newsitem.title: AFGHANISTAN: Afghan Taleban say civilian evacuation temporary.
newsitem.headline: Afghan Taleban say civilian evacuation temporary.

text.p: Afghanistan's Islamist Taleban will keep civilians out of areas the militia has captured north of Kabul until all weapons have been removed, an official said on Wednesday.

"Our decision is not to allow refugees to come back for the time being as we have not finished cleaning up the areas from armed people," said Mir Zaa Ahmad, deputy commander of the Taleban police and security department in the town of Charikar.

Thousands of people have fled their homes in Charikar and other towns north of Kabul after the Taleban retook the area on January 16. Many have headed for Kabul in hopes of finding friends or relatives who can help them stay alive at the height of a bitterly cold winter.

The Taleban, which captured Kabul last September, is now advancing into northern territory held by an alliance between former government military chief Ahmad Shah Masood and northern Uzbek leader General Abdul Rashid Dostum.
Ahmad told Reuters that Taleban fighters had collected around 240 modern weapons in Charikar, which lies about 60 km (37.5 miles) north of Kabul and is mostly populated by Masood's ethnic Tajiks.
Dozens of heavy machine guns, mortar and anti-aircraft shell bullets were piled outside Charikar's police headquarters.
Even two ancient muzzle-loading guns used for hunting which were brought in by Taleban fighters were deemed dangerous and Ahmad ordered them added to the pile.
"Carrying or keeping a gun is not allowed under Taleban rule, whether it is antique or not. We want to finish corruption and collecting guns from people is our main task," he said.
The Taleban routinely refer to Masood's forces as "the corrupt".
Some of the few thousand people left in Charikar gathered at the police headquarters on Wednesday, most of them elderly and begging for permission to bring back their families.
One old man just wanted to go back to his home, saying he hoped he would get permission because he had no sons who could be a danger to the Taleban.
There was no immediate word on whether an exception would be made for him.
Ahmad told Reuters that people would be allowed to return when the Taleban were confident they had collected all the weapons.
He said he did not know how long that would take.
